Homemade Clam Chowder Recipe – Warm, Cozy & Packed with Flavor

This homemade clam chowder is creamy, cozy, and packed with delicious flavor in every spoonful. Made with tender potatoes, savory bacon, chopped clams, and a rich creamy broth, this easy stovetop soup is perfect for a comforting lunch or dinner. You’ll love how simple it is to make this restaurant-style clam chowder at home using easy ingredients and one pot!

Why You’ll Love Clam Chowder

  • This clam chowder is rich, creamy, and so comforting. It has tender potatoes, savory bacon, and delicious clams in every bite. The creamy broth makes it taste like a restaurant-style soup made right at home. It is perfect for a cozy lunch or dinner.
  • This recipe is easy to make on the stovetop. Everything cooks in one pot, which keeps the process simple. You do not need any fancy ingredients or complicated steps. It is a great recipe for home cooks who want a homemade soup without a lot of effort.
  • Canned clams make this clam chowder extra convenient. They are easy to use and add great seafood flavor to the soup. The reserved clam juice also helps make the broth taste even better. This is a simple way to get that classic clam chowder flavor at home.
  • The bacon adds amazing flavor to this chowder. It gives the soup a smoky, savory taste that goes so well with the creamy broth. You also use a little bacon fat to cook the onion and garlic, which makes the base even more delicious. The crispy bacon on top adds the perfect finishing touch.
  • This clam chowder is hearty enough to be a full meal. The potatoes make it filling, while the clams add protein and flavor. Serve it with bread, crackers, or a simple salad for an easy dinner. It is a wonderful recipe for chilly days or whenever you want something warm and satisfying.

Ingredients For Clam Chowder

  • Bacon – Adds a smoky, savory flavor to the clam chowder. It also becomes a crispy topping for serving.
  • Unsalted butter – Helps cook the onion and garlic. It also adds richness to the creamy soup base.
  • Garlic – Gives the chowder a delicious savory flavor. Fresh minced garlic works best for this recipe.
  • Onion – Adds sweetness and depth to the soup. As it cooks, it softens and blends into the creamy broth.
  • Dried thyme – Adds classic cozy soup flavor. It pairs so well with the potatoes, clams, and creamy broth.
  • All-purpose flour – Helps thicken the chowder. It gives the soup that rich, creamy texture.
  • Milk – Adds creaminess to the broth without making it too heavy. It helps create the base of the chowder.
  • Vegetable stock – Adds flavor and liquid to the soup. It works together with the clam juice to make a tasty broth.
  • Chopped clams – The star ingredient in this clam chowder. Canned chopped clams make this recipe easy and convenient.
  • Reserved clam juice – Adds extra clam flavor to the soup. Be sure to save the juice from the cans before adding the clams.
  • Bay leaf – Adds subtle savory flavor while the soup simmers. Remove it before serving.
  • Russet potatoes – Make the chowder hearty and filling. They also help thicken the soup as they cook.
  • Half and half – Makes the chowder rich, creamy, and smooth. You can add a little more if you want a thinner texture.
  • Salt – Brings out all the flavors in the soup. Start with the recipe amount and adjust if needed.
  • Black pepper – Adds a little warmth and seasoning. Freshly ground black pepper is a great choice.
  • Fresh parsley – Adds color and freshness on top. It makes the finished clam chowder look bright and delicious.

For the exact measurements of the ingredients, see the printable recipe card at the bottom of this article.

How To Make Clam Chowder

  • Cook the diced bacon in a Dutch oven or large stockpot over medium-high heat until it is brown and crispy. Remove the bacon and set it aside on a paper towel-lined plate.
  • Melt the butter in the same pot with a little bacon fat. Add the onion and garlic, then cook until the onion is soft and translucent.
  • Stir in the dried thyme and flour. Cook for about a minute so the flour can lightly brown and help thicken the chowder.
  • Slowly whisk in the milk, vegetable stock, reserved clam juice, and bay leaf. Keep whisking until the broth starts to thicken.
  • Add the diced potatoes and bring the soup to a boil. Lower the heat and let it simmer until the potatoes are tender.
  • Stir in the half and half and chopped clams. Let everything heat through for a couple of minutes.
  • Season the chowder with salt and black pepper. Add a little extra half and half if you want the soup thinner and creamier.
  • Remove the bay leaf and ladle the clam chowder into bowls. Top with crispy bacon and fresh parsley before serving.

Serving Suggestions

  • Serve this creamy clam chowder with mini baguette, cheesy garlic bread, or homemade dinner rolls. The bread is perfect for dipping into the rich, flavorful broth.
  • Pair it with oyster crackers, saltine crackers, or buttery crackers for a classic soup topping. They add a nice crunch to every creamy spoonful.
  • Enjoy it with a green goddess salad, cucumber, tomato, and scallion salad, or apple coleslaw on the side. The fresh vegetables balance the richness of the chowder.
  • Serve the chowder with roasted brussels sprouts, baked potatoes, or steamed broccoli for a heartier meal. These easy sides make the soup feel even more filling.
  • Top each bowl with crispy baked bacon, chopped parsley, green onions, or shredded Parmesan cheese. These toppings add extra flavor, color, and texture.
  • Make it a cozy seafood dinner with avocado shrimp egg salad, homemade crab cakes, or baked swai fish. These recipes pair well with the creamy clam flavor.

Tips For Success

  • When making clam chowder, one of the best tips is to save the clam juice from the canned clams. Do not drain it into the sink. This juice adds so much delicious clam flavor to the soup and helps make the broth taste rich and savory. Add the clams themselves near the end of cooking so they stay tender and do not get overcooked.
  • Be sure to cook the bacon first and save a little of the bacon fat in the pot. This gives the onions and garlic so much flavor as they cook. You do not need a lot of bacon fat, just enough to help create a tasty base for the chowder. The crispy bacon also makes a wonderful topping, so set it aside until serving instead of stirring it in too early.
  • Dice the potatoes into small, even pieces so they cook at the same time. If the potato pieces are too large, they will take longer to become tender. Smaller pieces also make the chowder easier to eat and help the soup thicken nicely. Russet potatoes work well because they become soft and creamy as they simmer.
  • When adding the milk, stock, and clam juice, pour them in slowly while whisking. This helps the flour mix smoothly into the liquid and keeps the chowder from becoming lumpy. Keep whisking until the soup starts to thicken slightly. Once the potatoes are added, let the chowder simmer gently until they are tender.
  • Do not boil the chowder hard after adding the half and half. A gentle heat is best for keeping the creamy broth smooth. The clams only need a minute or two to warm through, so add them at the end. Taste the soup before serving and adjust the salt and black pepper if needed. Finish each bowl with crispy bacon and fresh parsley for the best flavor and presentation.

Variations And Substitutions

  • This clam chowder is delicious as written, but there are easy ways to adjust it based on what you have in your kitchen. If you want even more seafood flavor, add an extra can of chopped clams. Be sure to include the reserved clam juice too, because it adds so much flavor to the creamy broth. You can also use bottled clam juice in place of some of the vegetable stock if you want a stronger clam taste.
  • For the potatoes, russet potatoes make the chowder creamy and hearty. You can also use Yukon gold potatoes if that is what you have. Yukon gold potatoes hold their shape a little more, so the texture will be slightly different but still delicious. Dice the potatoes small so they cook evenly and fit nicely on the spoon.
  • If you do not have half and half, you can use a mix of milk and heavy cream. This keeps the chowder rich and creamy. For a lighter version, use more milk, but the soup may not be quite as thick. If the chowder gets too thick, stir in a splash of milk, half and half, or stock until it reaches the texture you like.
  • You can also change the toppings. Crispy bacon and parsley are classic, but green onions, chives, shredded cheese, or oyster crackers are tasty too. For a little extra flavor, sprinkle a bit more black pepper on top before serving. A dash of hot sauce can also be added to individual bowls for a little kick.
  • To make this clam chowder without bacon, skip the bacon and cook the onion and garlic in butter instead. The flavor will be milder, but still creamy and comforting. You may want to add a little extra salt or seasoning to make up for the missing bacon. This is a helpful option for anyone who does not eat bacon but still wants a cozy homemade clam chowder.

Storage and Reheating

  • Store leftover clam chowder in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Let the chowder cool before putting it away, but do not leave it sitting out for too long.
  • Reheat the chowder gently on the stovetop over low heat, stirring often, until it is hot. Try not to boil it, since the creamy broth can separate if it gets too hot too quickly.
  • You can also reheat individual portions in the microwave. Place the chowder in a microwave-safe bowl and heat in short intervals, stirring between each one, until warmed through.
  • If the chowder thickens in the refrigerator, stir in a splash of milk, half and half, or vegetable stock while reheating. This will help bring back the creamy soup texture.
  • Freezing is not recommended for this clam chowder. Cream-based soups can separate after freezing and thawing, and the potatoes may become grainy.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use fresh clams instead of canned clams?

Yes, you can use fresh clams to make clam chowder. Canned clams are very convenient and make this recipe quick and easy, but fresh clams are a delicious option too. If using fresh clams, chop them before adding them to the soup. You will also need clam juice for the broth, since canned clams come with reserved juice that adds flavor. Fresh clams may need a little extra cooking time, so make sure they are fully cooked before serving. The flavor will be fresh, savory, and delicious.

Can I use frozen clams for this recipe?

Yes, frozen clams can be used in this clam chowder. Thaw them completely before adding them to the soup. Since many frozen clams are already cooked, add them near the end of the recipe just like canned clams. This helps keep them tender and prevents them from becoming rubbery. Make sure they are heated through before serving. You may also want to use bottled clam juice or extra stock to replace the juice that normally comes from canned clams.

Why is my clam chowder too thick?

Clam chowder can thicken as it cooks, especially because this recipe uses flour and russet potatoes. Russet potatoes are starchy, so they help make the chowder creamy and hearty. If your chowder is thicker than you like, stir in a splash of milk, half and half, or vegetable stock. Add a little at a time until the soup reaches your preferred texture. It is best to do this slowly so you do not make the chowder too thin. The chowder may also thicken more after being refrigerated, so you can thin leftovers when reheating.

Why is my clam chowder too thin?

If your clam chowder is too thin, let it simmer a little longer before adding the clams and half and half. Simmering helps the potatoes soften and the broth reduce slightly. The flour also needs a little time to thicken the soup. Make sure the flour is whisked well into the butter, onion, and garlic mixture before adding the liquids. If the soup still seems thin, continue cooking gently until it reaches the texture you like. Keep in mind that the chowder will thicken slightly as it cools.

Can I make this clam chowder ahead of time?

Yes, clam chowder can be made ahead of time and stored in the refrigerator. It is a great soup to prepare earlier in the day or the day before serving. Store it in an airtight container once it has cooled. When reheating, warm it gently over low heat and stir often. Do not boil the chowder after reheating, because the creamy broth can separate. Add a splash of milk, half and half, or stock if it becomes too thick.

Can I freeze clam chowder?

Freezing is not recommended for this creamy clam chowder. Cream-based soups can separate after freezing and thawing. The potatoes may also change texture and become grainy or mushy. For the best taste and texture, store leftovers in the refrigerator and eat them within a few days. If you need to make it ahead, refrigerating is the better choice. Reheat slowly so the chowder stays smooth and creamy.

What should I serve with clam chowder?

Clam chowder is delicious with bread, crackers, or a fresh salad. Crusty bread, garlic bread, or dinner rolls are great for dipping into the creamy broth. Oyster crackers or saltine crackers add a classic crunchy topping. A simple green salad, cucumber tomato salad, or coleslaw adds freshness and balances the richness of the soup. You can also serve it with roasted vegetables or baked potatoes for a heartier meal. For a seafood-style dinner, pair it with shrimp salad, crab cakes, or baked fish.

How do I keep the clams tender?

Add the clams near the end of cooking and heat them only until warmed through. Canned clams are already cooked, so they do not need a long cooking time. If they simmer too long, they can become chewy. Stir them in after the potatoes are tender and after the half and half has been added. Let them warm for just a minute or two before serving. This keeps the clams soft, tender, and flavorful.

Clam Chowder

This homemade clam chowder is rich, creamy, and full of comforting flavor. Tender potatoes, savory bacon, chopped clams, and a creamy broth come together in one pot for an easy soup that tastes like it came from a restaurant. This cozy clam chowder is perfect for lunch, dinner, or serving with crusty bread on a chilly day.
Prep Time15 minutes mins
Cook Time30 minutes mins
Total Time45 minutes mins
Course: Main Dish, Soup
Cuisine: American
Keyword: canned clam chowder, clam chowder, creamy clam chowder, easy clam chowder, homemade clam chowder, New England clam chowder
Cooking Method: Stovetop
Diet: Pescatarian
Servings: 6
Calories: 254kcal
Author: MelanieCooks.com

Ingredients

  • 4 bacon slices, diced
  • 2 tbsp unsalted butter
  • 2 cloves garlic minced
  • 1 onion diced
  • 1/2 tbsp dried thyme
  • 3 tbsp all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup milk
  • 1 cup vegetable stock
  • 2 cans clams chopped, 6.5 ounces each, juices reserved
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 2 russet potatoes peeled and diced
  • 1 cup half and half
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/4 tsp black pepper
  • 2 tbsp fresh parsley chopped

Instructions

  • Heat a Dutch oven or large stockpot over medium-high heat. Add the diced bacon and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, or until browned and crispy. Transfer the bacon to a paper towel-lined plate and leave about 1 tablespoon of bacon fat in the pot.
  • Add the butter to the pot and let it melt. Add the garlic and onion and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring often, until the onion softens.
  • Stir in the dried thyme and cook for 1 minute. Add the flour and whisk for about 1 minute, until lightly golden.
  • Slowly whisk in the milk, vegetable stock, reserved clam juice, and bay leaf. Continue whisking for 1 to 2 minutes, until the soup begins to thicken slightly.
  • Stir in the diced potatoes. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender.
  • Stir in the half and half and chopped clams. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, just until heated through.
  • Add the salt and black pepper. If the chowder is too thick, stir in a little more half and half until it reaches your desired consistency.
  • Remove the bay leaf. Serve hot, topped with the crispy bacon and fresh parsley.

Notes

  • For extra clam flavor, use an additional can of chopped clams and include the reserved juice.
  • The cooking time may vary depending on how small or large the potatoes are diced.
